feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/663e4d77d51816641a9fa861f37893d9f986d5e2b00e605ed5eb4fc19d40eab4.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})≈(5,5)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})≈(7,9).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{9-5}{7-5} \\  & =\frac{4}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=2$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=2x+b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(5,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2x+b \\ 5 & =2(5)+b \\ 5 & =10+b \\ -5 & =b \\ b & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=2x-5.
$$
